A job listing from Apple suggests the company may be planning to roll out some live classes for Apple Fitness+. However, I have strong doubts that things are exactly as they seem.

The position is for a studio producer, and Apple specifically wants candidates with extensive live production experience and a "sincere curiosity about the future of live content"...

MacRumors discovered the listing several weeks after it was posted, and it does contain a number of references to "live".

Apple Fitness+ is looking for a producer with a strong live or live-to-tape multi-camera production background and a sincere curiosity about the future of live content. We want to find a creative collaborator who is passionate about experimenting with new formats, pushing the boundaries of live fitness content, helping to shape the next generation of the Fitness+ experience—while also being able to establish and maintain a constantly changing, fluid production schedule that keeps pace with the rhythms of the live production environment. If you thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment and want to join a collaborative, innovative team that is redefining live production at Apple, this is your chance to shine.

Some of the requirements also point in this direction.

  • Equally comfortable with live and post-production workflows, able to switch seamlessly between the two
  • Must be able to adapt to a control room, office environment, as well as live on-site settings

Even so, it's hard to see what advantage live Fitness+ classes would have over pre-recorded ones. Since the pandemic, even Apple's keynotes have relied on pre-recorded video segments; while some may miss the thrill of a live address, the prevailing view is that this approach delivers a better experience.

At most, I could imagine some kind of real-time event held on special occasions, but I still expect the actual fitness classes to be pre-recorded. I think the biggest clue is the phrase "the rhythms of the live production environment," along with the willingness to accept live-to-tape experience. I believe Apple wants to capture that exciting live feel even for pre-recorded content.

What do you think? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
